instruction: I'm developing a Tetris game in Python. When the game ends, it just stops without any notification. Please add a game over screen in main.py that displays 'Game Over' message when the game state is 'gameover', and allows players to press 'R' to restart the game.

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding game over screen and restart functionality in main.py. Implementation needs: (1) check for game.state == 'gameover', (2) display 'Game Over' text using render/blit, (3) handle R key press for restart, (4) reset game state by creating new Tetris instance. Evaluator checks for all four components with partial credit scoring.

llm_judge_reasons: Check 1 uses overly loose keyword matching: '(game AND state)' will match any occurrence of these common words, not specifically 'game.state == gameover' condition
Check 2 doesn't verify that 'Game Over' text and render/blit are used together in the correct context (when game state is gameover)
Check 4 has very weak verification: '(game AND = AND tetris)' pattern will match unrelated code or comments, not specifically verifying new Tetris instance creation on restart
No verification of conditional logic or proper integration: the four elements could exist in the file but not be logically connected
Keyword-based matching lacks context awareness and will produce false positives for incorrect implementations
Check 3 (K_R key detection) is the only relatively robust check
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use AST parsing to verify actual code structure instead of simple keyword matching
Check for specific patterns like 'if game.state == "gameover"' or 'if self.state == "gameover"' instead of just looking for 'game' and 'state' keywords
Verify that render/blit calls for 'Game Over' text occur within the gameover state conditional block
Check for specific restart pattern like 'game = Tetris()' or 'self.__init__()' when K_R is pressed, not just presence of keywords
Add verification that the restart logic is inside an event handler for the R key press
Consider using regex patterns to match actual Python syntax rather than loose keyword searches
